preamble: Thirteen solutions are of a kind and have partial clues.

clue.text: Treat maybe with stories about storm

parts.note: re is the short Latin-derived word meaning concerning
a gale is a strong wind, a stormy blow

explanation.surface: Someone treats a listener by telling tales about a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'stories': to regale someone is to treat them, often with anecdotes; 'maybe' flags that treating with stories is one kind of regaling.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale is to entertain lavishly, typically by pouring out amusing anecdotes or feasting a guest.

clue.text: Buttons for Glenn

parts.note: Red Buttons was an American comic actor, so his first name stands in
Glenn Ford was a Hollywood star, so his surname completes the pair

explanation.surface: It reads like a sewing note: buttons set aside for someone called Glenn.
explanation.walkthrough: The preamble says thirteen answers share a kind: they are surnames of film actors, here Robert Redford. Each clue word is half of another actor's name, and the clue supplies the missing halves.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Redford is a celebrated Hollywood film star, one of the thirteen actors the preamble groups together.

clue.text: This is on the house

parts.note: surface reading: a free drink, something the pub gives away
setter's reading: a triangular end-wall that literally sits on a building

explanation.walkthrough: 'On the house' is the idiom for free of charge, but here it is literal: the triangular top of a house wall. The preamble makes the answer an actor too, Clark Gable.
explanation.definitionFit: A gable is the triangular upper part of a wall beneath a pitched roof, and Clark Gable was a leading Hollywood star.

clue.text: The rose-red city

parts.note: surface reading: the famous poetic description of Petra, the ancient Jordanian city
setter's reading: the city whose royal house took a red rose as its emblem

explanation.walkthrough: 'A rose-red city half as old as time' is a well-known line about Petra, which you are meant to think of. The English House of Lancaster's badge was the red rose, opposed to York's white in the Wars of the Roses; the actor is Burt Lancaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is the English city linked with the red-rose badge of its royal house, and Burt Lancaster was a Hollywood star.

clue.text: The guy whose love is returned

parts.note: a chap is an informal word for a man or fellow

indicators.note: something returned is sent back the way it came, so these letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, hence nil

explanation.surface: A man is lucky enough to have his love requited.
explanation.walkthrough: Love requited is the picture, but 'returned' only means written backwards. The actor is Charlie Chaplin, of silent comedy fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlie Chaplin was the silent-film comedian famous as the Tramp, one of the thirteen actors the preamble groups.

clue.text: Mould for game on railway or beach, say

indicators.note: 'say' means as spoken, so what follows is judged by how the words sound out loud

parts.note: chess is a board game
EL is short for elevated railway, as in Chicago
Chesil Beach is a long shingle bank on the Dorset coast

explanation.surface: A sand mould to shape a game on a railway or a beach, like a child's toy.
explanation.walkthrough: Two routes to one word: CHESS plus EL builds it, and it also sounds like Chesil, the famous English shingle beach in Dorset.
explanation.definitionFit: A chessel is a cheese-making vessel, a container in which curds are pressed and shaped into cheeses.

clue.text: Confused by scene of more regrettable events

definitions.meaning: first meaning: bewildered, not knowing what to do
second meaning: the proverb says worse things happen on the ocean

explanation.surface: Someone is bewildered by a place where worse things keep happening.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half alludes to the consoling British saying 'worse things happen at sea', used to cheer someone after a mishap.
explanation.definitionFit: Being lost on the ocean is an idiom for bewilderment, and the proverb names the ocean as the place where worse things happen.

clue.text: What Bohemian king did seemed to call for raised finger

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in the carol, Good King Wenceslas of Bohemia gazed from his window on the feast of Stephen

definitions.text: seemed to call for raised finger
definitions.meaning: second meaning: seemed (looked) plus the cricket decision an umpire signals by lifting a finger

explanation.surface: A Bohemian monarch's behaviour apparently demanded a raised finger, as if he were being told off.
explanation.walkthrough: The Christmas carol begins 'Good King Wenceslas looked out'. In cricket an umpire raises one finger to give a batsman out, so 'seemed' plus that call reads the same.
explanation.definitionFit: The carol's first line gives the king's action, and the cricket umpire's raised finger signals a dismissal, combined with seemed.

clue.text: Where modern pictures are heard to drop off?

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by the ear, so only the sound of the words matters

parts.note: Tate Modern is London's gallery of modern art, a newer Tate

explanation.surface: Visitors to a gallery of modern art supposedly nod off.
explanation.walkthrough: Tate Modern is the London gallery of modern art, the new Tate; said out loud that gives the answer. 'Drop off' wants to mean fall asleep, but here it is nodding the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To nutate is to nod or droop, as a dozing head or a flower stem bends downward.

clue.text: Low beast being identified?

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog, a contemptible creature
'tis is 'it is', the words used to identify someone, as in 'tis I

explanation.surface: Some lowly animal is being picked out in an identity parade.
explanation.walkthrough: Old poetic 'tis contracts 'it is', the phrase of identification. The actor is Tony Curtis.
explanation.definitionFit: Tony Curtis was a Hollywood leading man, star of Some Like It Hot, one of the thirteen grouped actors.

clue.text: Bond in river at junction with river

parts.note: the Deben is a river in Suffolk, England
a T-junction is where one road meets another at right angles
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone is tied up in a river where it meets another river.
explanation.walkthrough: Both rivers are small English ones: the Deben in Suffolk and the Ure in Yorkshire. 'At' and 'with' simply line the pieces up.
explanation.definitionFit: A debenture is a long-term loan certificate issued by a company, a kind of bond secured on its assets.

clue.text: Great writer?

parts.note: surface reading: an outstanding author
setter's reading: the word that follows 'Great' in an old exclamation of surprise, which is also the surname of the author of Ivanhoe

explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Scott!' is an old exclamation, and Sir Walter Scott wrote Ivanhoe; the actor is George C. Scott, who played Patton.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Scott was a major novelist, the exclamation completes 'Great', and George C. Scott was a film star.

clue.text: Horse for Western at work on time

definitions.note: partial: horse opera is slang for a cowboy film

parts.note: op is short for opus, a musical work
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A cowboy's horse is at work in a film, right on schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: This is one of the partial clues: 'Horse' plus the answer makes 'horse opera', a jokey name for a cowboy film. 'On' just sets the work piece on top of the time piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse opera is slang for a Western film, so the missing word completes that idiom.

clue.text: Will's books

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a legal document disposing of property after death
second meaning: one of the two divisions of the Bible, Old or New

explanation.surface: Somebody named Will owns a few books, perhaps Shakespeare's.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will's' looks like a possessive, perhaps Shakespeare's, but it is 'Will is'. A last will and testament is the legal phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a legal will, and each Testament of the Bible is a collection of scriptural books.

clue.text: Discusses planting willow in rivers

indicators.note: planting puts something into the ground, so one piece is set inside another

parts.note: the Dee is a river name found in Scotland, Wales and England
cricket bats are made of willow

explanation.surface: Someone talks about putting willow trees along riverbanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Willow is the wood of a cricket bat, so the word stands for the bat itself.
explanation.definitionFit: To debate is to discuss a question by arguing the various sides, so discusses is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Spooner's to be united with anorak

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the first sounds of two words trade places

parts.note: to marry is to be joined in wedlock; its opening sound is swapped with the next word's
an anorak is British slang for an obsessive, tedious enthusiast

explanation.surface: Spooner announces he will wed a dull hobbyist.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the M and B of 'marry bore' gives the actor's name; the Barrymores were a famous acting family, John, Lionel and Ethel.
explanation.definitionFit: The Barrymores were a celebrated American acting dynasty, John Barrymore being a great stage and film star.

clue.text: One heard to get squeezed

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by the ear, so only the sound matters

parts.note: the 'one' to be squeezed is a citrus fruit, pressed for its juice

explanation.surface: Someone has heard they are about to be put under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: The fruit and the actor's name sound alike; Jack Lemmon starred in Some Like It Hot.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack Lemmon was a Hollywood comic and dramatic actor, one of the thirteen actors in the theme.

clue.text: Mix magnesium with deuterium (not uranium) in psychological warfare

indicators.note: to mix is to stir things together so their order is lost
'not' says the following item is excluded from the letters used

parts.note: taken as written
D is the chemical symbol for deuterium, heavy hydrogen
U is the chemical symbol for uranium, the letter removed

explanation.surface: A chemistry recipe for a weapon becomes an instruction in a psychological battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The trap is reading 'magnesium' as its symbol MG; it is used whole, while deuterium and uranium shrink to their symbols.
explanation.definitionFit: Mind games are manipulative tactics meant to unsettle or confuse an opponent, the essence of psychological warfare.

clue.text: I won't leave Goodwood for uninteresting nonsense

parts.note: dry means dull and boring
rot is British slang for rubbish talk

explanation.surface: A racegoer vows never to leave Goodwood for something dull and silly.
explanation.walkthrough: Goodwood is an English racecourse in Sussex, but split it into 'good wood': the fungus that decays timber will not leave wood sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay that destroys timber, so it leaves no sound timber behind, speaking in first person.

clue.text: Take in kitten playing with little shiny object

indicators.note: playing suggests frolicking about, so the letters move freely

parts.note: taken as written
R abbreviates Latin recipe, take, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone adopts a kitten that plays with a little shiny bauble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' wants to mean adopt, but 'Take' is the prescription R, and the kitten's letters rearrange around it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket is a small ornament or piece of jewellery of little value, often glittering.

clue.text: Artisan in the making

indicators.note: something in the making is still being formed, so its letters are not yet settled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A craftsman is still being trained, a work in progress.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor is Frank Sinatra, an Oscar winner for From Here to Eternity as well as a singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank Sinatra was a film actor as well as a singer, winning an Oscar, one of the thirteen grouped actors.

clue.text: Girl from Australia (wrong end)

parts.note: surface reading: a young woman who comes from that country
setter's reading: Australians call a girl this, and Australia is jokingly the far, upside-down end of the globe

explanation.walkthrough: Australian slang calls any girl or woman by this name; the bracket is a jokey aside that Australia lies at the 'wrong end' of the world, down under.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a sheila is any girl or woman, from the common Irish female name.

clue.text: A way to get higher direction

parts.note: taken as written
a stair is a means of climbing up
E is east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Advice on how to receive better guidance, or climb higher.
explanation.walkthrough: The actor is Fred Astaire, famous for dancing, fittingly up and down staircases in his films.
explanation.definitionFit: Fred Astaire was a Hollywood dancer and actor, one of the thirteen grouped film stars.

clue.text: Vegetables for stock at one's house, say?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: yellow root vegetables, rutabagas

definitions.note: people of one nation, as when one says Swede's house
definitions.meaning: second meaning: people of Scandinavian stock, one of whom owns the house

explanation.surface: Someone keeps root vegetables to make stock at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like soup stock but means ancestry; the Scandinavian nationals share their name with the vegetable, also known as rutabaga in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are rutabaga roots, and also natives of Sweden, a national stock of people.

clue.text: The things one does when partner swallows a fly — O bother!

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a wife is a marriage partner

indicators.note: to bother is to upset or disturb, so these letters are disturbed

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A spouse accidentally swallows an insect, and someone exclaims in exasperation.
explanation.walkthrough: It echoes the nursery song about the old lady who swallowed a fly. 'O bother!' sounds like a sigh, but the O joins the fodder and 'bother' stirs it.
explanation.definitionFit: A way of life is the habitual manner in which someone lives, the things they routinely do.

clue.text: Article follows with love

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the first item goes at the end

parts.note: fond means loving or affectionate
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A letter or item is sent on, signed off with love.
explanation.walkthrough: The actors are Henry Fonda and his children Jane and Peter.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry Fonda was a Hollywood star of Twelve Angry Men, one of the thirteen grouped actors.

clue.text: Better than a loan?

parts.note: surface reading: some financial arrangement preferable to borrowing
setter's reading: money given that never needs paying back

explanation.walkthrough: A student's award that need not be repaid beats borrowing; the actor is Cary Grant.
explanation.definitionFit: A grant is a sum of money awarded outright, unlike a loan, and Cary Grant was a Hollywood star.

clue.text: Something for any of the thirteen separately

definitions.text: Something for any of the thirteen
definitions.meaning: first meaning: a role, which every film actor needs, split into two words
second meaning: individually, at a distance from one another

explanation.surface: Each of the thirteen gets something of their own, handed over one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: The thirteen are the themed actors from the preamble, and what any actor wants is a role, read as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it is an acting role, and as one word it means separated or individually.

clue.text: Don't let anyone hear the doctor's confession?

definitions.note: an imperative phrase defining a verb

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
to own is to admit, so owning up is confessing

explanation.surface: A doctor's admission ought to stay confidential, unheard by others.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor-patient confidentiality is the picture; really the sense is to drown out a sound so nobody hears it.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown a sound is to make it inaudible by louder noise, stopping others from catching it.

clue.text: Mark enters desert when it's not hot with chintzy fabric

indicators.note: to enter is to go inside, so one piece sits within another
'when it's not' describes the item minus something, so a letter goes

parts.note: the Kalahari is a desert in southern Africa
H stands for hot, as on taps
MK abbreviates mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A person called Mark heads into the desert when it is cool, carrying gaudy cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' looks like a man's name; it is the old German currency. A desert that is not hot loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: Kalamkari is a hand-painted or block-printed Indian cotton textile, the kind that chintz descends from.

clue.text: Partners in opening

parts.note: a start is a beginning or opening
East and West are partners in bridge

explanation.surface: Partners join in at the opening of something.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the players sit as North-South and East-West pairs. The actor is James Stewart.
explanation.definitionFit: James Stewart was a Hollywood star of It's a Wonderful Life, one of the thirteen grouped actors.

clue.text: Fly from three sets

indicators.note: 'from' says the letters wanted are taken out of a longer string, the rest left behind

parts.note: the word written three times running

explanation.surface: Someone escapes from three sets, perhaps of tennis.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 'set' three times, SETSETSET, and the fly sits in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The tsetse is an African fly that feeds on blood and transmits sleeping sickness.
